{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts lag behind price turning points, underestimating bull market momentum and overestimating bear market declines.",
    "Sentiment indicators show positive bias when prices are near support levels and turn negative at resistance, predicting short-term reversals.",
    "When sentiment switches from negative to positive, model forecasts are too conservative and need 2-3 day catch-up to match actual price movement.",
    "Mean reversion bias in model forecasts causes undershoot of price extremes, especially in the first 50% of the forecast horizon.",
    "Sentiment strength correlates with forecast accuracy - strong sentiment signals (1.0 or -1.0) require 10-20% more extreme forecast values.",
    "Model uses constant volatility assumptions that understate price movement when sentiment is extreme, causing 0.5-1.0 Euro/day forecast errors.",
    "Forecasts become more accurate after day 15 in the 30-day horizon as volatility normalizes and sentiment effects decay."
] }
